stories.title: Florio, Simms apologize for comments about Vrabel's mustache in Germany
stories.summary: "PFT Live" hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms apologized for comments they made about Mike Vrabel's mustache when talking about the Patriots' trip to Germany.
stories.detail: Mike Florio and Chris Simms, hosts of the "PFT Live" podcast, apologized for comments they made on a recent episode about New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel's mustache during the team's recent trip to Germany. Florio, responding to Simms saying Vrabel has a "German mustache," said "you have to be careful trimming that thing" in an apparent allusion to the mustache of Adolf Hitler before defending the comment saying "it's funny ... it was 80 years ago, let's have some fun for crying out loud." While apparently alluding to Hitler, neither host said his name. "On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize," Florio and Simms said in a statement released by NBC Sports on Wednesday. Jeff Miller, the NFL's executive vice president of communications and public affairs, said in a statement: "We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive."

stories.title: Niners' Nick Bosa on 4-game sack drought: 'Don't think I'm playing my best'
stories.summary: Niners star Nick Bosa acknowledged his performance this season, including four straight games with no sacks, hasn't been up to his usual standard.
stories.detail: COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. -- After failing to record a sack in his fourth straight game, San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa acknowledged Wednesday that his performance this season has not been up to his usual standard. In the Niners' 46-40 win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Bosa played 34 defensive snaps in which he had a pass rush opportunity. He finished with no sacks, one quarterback hit and four pressures while also being called for three penalties, including two for jumping offside. It's the first time since Bosa entered the league in 2019 that he hasn't had a sack in four straight games in the same season. "I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said after the Niners completed their first practice of the week at the Air Force Academy in preparation for this week's showdown with the Minnesota Vikings . "But now I'm really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats. But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now. So that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats." Bosa is still working his way…

stories.title: Cam Skattebo done with backflip celebration in wake of Aidan Hutchinson injury
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo has seen enough. The Giants RB says he is ending his backflip celebration in the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending injury.
stories.detail: No flipping way. That's the message from New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo in regard to his famed touchdown celebration. Skattebo, who has never been one to shy away from contact or a moment to celebrate, saw all he needed to see when it came to Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending injury . The Detroit Lions ' star celebrated a sack of New England Patriots QB Drake Maye by jumping in the air. When Hutchinson landed, he suffered a torn ACL. And that was enough for Skattebo to retire his backflip celebration – at least for the time being. “It’s hard to see,” Skattebo told reporters, via the New York Post's Ryan Dunleavy , after Wednesday’s practice. “I’m saying yeah (no more). Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” This isn't the first time that the running back's celebration has been a topic of discussion. Skattebo was seen on video backflipping multiple times last offseason, despite coming off a serious season-ending ankle injury in 2025. It got to a point where new head coach, John Harbaugh, was asked for his reaction. Harbaugh joked about the situation, saying in part, " Dude, at least stick it ." The 24-year-old brought the celebration …

stories.title: Sixers' Tyrese Maxey (foot) late scratch vs. Magic
stories.summary: Already without Jaylen Brown, the Sixers also won't have guard Tyrese Maxey for Wednesday's game against the Magic because of right foot soreness.
stories.detail: ORLANDO, Fla. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey will miss Wednesday night's game against the Orlando Magic with right foot soreness, adding to a list of Sixers sidelined. The Sixers also will be without forwards Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade , who are both nursing left hamstring injuries. Maxey has been the engine of the Sixers, averaging a team-leading 26.5 points. He is also one of three players, along with Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope , to play in all 15 games this season. With Maxey and Brown out, the Sixers will be without their top two scorers; Brown is averaging 22.6 points and had a season high 31 in Monday's win over the Brooklyn Nets . Maxey wasn't on any of the Sixers injury reports, but the team downgraded him to questionable a little over an hour before tipoff, just before he ran out on the floor to warm up Wednesday night. After Maxey went through warmups, he spoke with Sixers' staffers on the team bench about his foot, and the Sixers ruled him out moments later. The Sixers will start VJ Edgecombe , Simons, Caldwell-Pope, LeBron James and Joel Embiid against the Magic, who are riding a four-game winning streak.

On Wednesday, Tom Friend of Sportsbusinessjournal.com reported that former Lakers star Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant are joining forces to place a bid for the WNBA team. Friend reported that Gasol declined to speak on the matter through a spokesperson and said, “Gasol16 Venture is always open to exploring investments.” One of Bryant’s representatives said, “She has not personally had any conversations with the Sparks.” Pau Gasol sitting courtside at a Lakers game during his jersey retirement ceremony. London Entertainment / SplashNews.com Bryant denied the report and said “False” on the rumored bid that was reported by The Sports Business Journal. “Another rumor out today… I’ve never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA team owner. If that was true, I would announce it,” Bryant wrote on an Instagram post. “I’m just over here undecided on what seasonal coffee flavor I like and over caffeinated… ” The relationship between Gasol and Bryant dates back to 2008, when he and her late husband, Kobe Bryant, were Lakers teammates. stories.title: Karl-Anthony Towns’ ‘bittersweet’ Minnesota return comes as a Knicks champion
stories.summary: “I wanted to win one there. I didn’t accomplish that,” Towns said.
stories.detail: KAT Return TORONTO — Karl-Anthony Towns is returning to Minnesota as an NBA champion , which solidifies the big trade as a Knicks victory but still feels “bittersweet” for the player. “I wanted to win one there. I didn’t accomplish that,” Towns said ahead of Thursday’s game against the Timberwolves. “But it was great to have those moments, to bring Minnesota back to the playoffs and be able to do a lot of things.” Towns spent nine seasons with the Timberwolves and served as the franchise star for most of them. There was a lot of losing but also an appearance in the conference finals, which was immediately followed by Towns’ departure to New York in a 2024 blockbuster. Although it often takes years to declare the winning side of a trade, this one can already be called in the Knicks’ favor: New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns smiles after receiving his championship ring before a game on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. stories.title: Miami Heat go all out with Vice City night ahead of 'Grand Theft Auto 6' release
stories.summary: Torrential rain in South Florida didn't deter fans from showing up for "A Night in Vice City." The Miami Heat gave them plenty to take in.
stories.detail: MIAMI — In this corner of Vice City, at least it was dry. Outside, torrential downpours that lasted all day and had threatened flooding throughout South Florida didn’t deter thousands of fans from lining up outside the Kaseya Center for a Miami Heat-Milwaukee Bucks game that was rebranded to celebrate the midnight release of "Grand Theft Auto 6." The game is set in a fictional city named Leonida, otherwise known as Vice City, that is very closely based on Miami. The video game franchise has a massive fan base and this one has been in production for more than a decade, leading to intense enthusiasm and anticipation for the latest release. Fans, donned in ponchos and raincoats being blasted by the wind, were lined up outside the Kaseya Center more than four hours before tipoff. Inside, the vibe was euphoric and festive, and the interest in the activations was overwhelming. A custom court with electric pink and blue paint matched the pink at center court, where “Vice City” was painted in the video game’s font. teamStories.summary: The Spurs ruled guard Dylan Harper out for Thursday's game against the Clippers due to left hip soreness following his slip on the court Tuesday.
teamStories.detail: SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs guard Dylan Harper will miss Thursday's home game against the LA Clippers due to left hip soreness. Harper left San Antonio's 105-93 loss to Detroit on Tuesday with 53 seconds remaining after slipping on the court. Harper's feet slid out from under him as he stopped to plant on a pass from Stephon Castle with 1:07 remaining in the game. Harper fell and remained on the court as Ausar Thompson stole the pass, helping preserve the Pistons' victory that snapped San Antonio's 12-game winning streak. Harper remained on the court for about a minute before the action was stopped by a San Antonio foul. He was helped off the court by teammates and staff. Harper finished with 20 points, four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes against Detroit. The second-year guard is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists while shooting 50.5% from the field.
